journey_control.additive_note: Journeys are additive by nature: this document is added to the Feature Design Package and is never merged into a canonical document. There is no delta, no version_bump and no canonical destination — which is why this agent, unlike the four viewpoint agents, does not run in delta mode.
journey_control.out_of_scope_rationale: Stated rather than omitted. A persona silently absent from a journey map reads as an oversight; a persona named with a reason reads as a decision.

journeys.title: Producer registers and waits for eligibility
journeys.trigger: A producer has heard about HarvestLink and wants to sell.
journeys.outcome_success: The producer is registered, verified, and can publish a listing.
journeys.outcome_failure: The producer is registered, rejected, and knows why and what to do next.

steps.action: Arrives at HarvestLink and chooses to sign up
steps.system_response: Redirected to the external identity provider
steps.emotional_note: Highest abandonment risk in the journey — the producer has no account yet and no investment in the outcome.

steps.system_response: Session established; returned to HarvestLink with a role provisioned from the onboarding record
steps.note: The producer never sees a Thornbury employee login. That is a hard boundary, not a design preference.

steps.action: Completes the registration form: business details, FBO number, attestation tick
steps.system_response: Field-level validation on the FBO number format
steps.emotional_note: The producer may not have their FBO number to hand. The journey must survive being abandoned here and resumed later.

steps.action: Reads and ticks the FBO-status attestation
steps.system_response: Submission refused if unticked — server-side, not merely hidden in the UI
steps.note: This is the step the whole facilitation-only regulatory position rests on. It is a deliberate act by an identified party, and the UI must not let it feel like boilerplate.

steps.action: Accepts the registration and holds it pending-verification
steps.system_response: Producer sees an explicit pending state with what happens next and roughly when
steps.emotional_note: The producer has finished their part and cannot act further. An unexplained wait here is read as failure.

steps.action: Attempts to publish a listing while still pending
steps.system_response: Publication blocked, with the reason stated as 'verification in progress', not as a generic permission error
steps.note: A blocked action that does not explain itself generates the support contact this step exists to prevent.

steps.system_response: Registration becomes valid, evidence recorded, publication permitted, producer notified
Registration rejected, producer notified with the reason, publication stays blocked
Registration stays pending and is retried; the producer sees the same pending state
steps.note: From the producer's side a timeout and a slow answer are indistinguishable, and deliberately so — an unknown eligibility must never be presented as a provisional yes.

touchpoints.name: Public landing
touchpoints.owning_component_note: Shares the public shell with the buyer experience; the producer path diverges at sign-up.

not_reached.reason: Duplicate verification delivery has no user-visible surface. Correctly absent from the journey — the producer cannot perceive a deduplicated event, and inventing a step for it would put a system concern in a persona's path.

findings.summary: Journey step 5 requires a registration status screen that no Work Unit builds.
findings.detail: TP-04 carries steps 5, 6 and 7b — the entire pending state, including the blocked-publication explanation. S-F1.1-a-AC4 covers the blocking behaviour, and WU-F1.1-04 implements the gate as business logic, but no Work Unit in tasks.json owns the producer-facing surface that shows it.
findings.resolution_note: Raised to task-generator and the cycle planner. This agent does not mint Work Units, and the alternative — quietly folding the status screen into WU-F1.1-03's registration form — would breach T1, since a form and a status screen are two nameable objectives.

findings.summary: The journey has no resumption path, and step 3 predicts abandonment.
findings.detail: A producer who does not have their FBO number to hand will leave the form. Nothing in the Cycle 1 stories describes what they return to — a saved draft, a fresh form, or a session that has expired.
findings.resolution_note: No acceptance criterion covers resumption and none was invented. Recorded for the story generator's next elaboration.

findings.summary: OQ-01 has a visible journey consequence.
findings.detail: Story-generator's open question — what happens when a verified registration later lapses — is not an abstract gap. It is a journey with no map: a producer who has published listings and whose registration then lapses appears nowhere in UJ-01, and the listings are already visible to buyers.
findings.resolution_note: Strengthens OQ-01 rather than answering it. Journey mapping surfaced a consequence the requirement did not state.

consistency_check.note: Every journey step's system_response was compared against the acceptance criterion it claims to cover. Step 7b was corrected during authoring: the draft had the status screen show 'verification delayed', which contradicts S-F1.1-b-AC3 — a producer told their verification is delayed has been told something the system does not know, and the pending state must be indistinguishable from a slow answer.

artifacts.name: user-journeys.md
artifacts.description: One producer journey across F5.1 and both F1.1 slices; 9 steps including two branches, 5 touchpoints, 3 findings

content.execution_summary:
• Mapped one journey, UJ-01, for the Producer persona across F5.1 and both F1.1 slices: 9 steps including a rejection branch and a timeout branch, over 5 touchpoints.
• Three personas were named as out of scope with reasons rather than omitted. A persona silently absent from a journey map is indistinguishable from one nobody thought about.
• Coverage: 10 of 11 in-scope acceptance criteria are reached by a journey step. S-F1.1-b-AC4 (duplicate verification delivery) is deliberately not reached — it has no user-visible surface, and inventing a step for it would put a system concern into a persona's path.
• Three findings, none resolved here. UJ-F01 is the substantive one: the journey needs a registration status screen that carries the pending state and the blocked-publication explanation, and no Work Unit builds it. Folding it into the registration form Work Unit would breach T1, so it is raised to task-generator rather than absorbed.
• UJ-F03 is worth the cycle planner's attention: story-generator's OQ-01 turns out to have a journey with no map behind it — a producer whose registration lapses after publishing has listings already visible to buyers, and nothing describes what they or the buyers see.
• Output is additive. It lands in the FDP's additive/ folder, is never merged into a canonical document, and emits no delta — which is why this agent does not run in delta mode as the four viewpoint agents do.
• Knowledge bases consulted: kb-L1-sdlc-templates (journey and touchpoint structure); kb-L2-food-domain via the persona records (FD2 participant model — a producer is UI-first and low-capability, which is why every step assumes a phone and no API).
• Guardrails evaluated: gr-L1-consistency-check (pass — one step corrected during authoring, where the draft told the producer their verification was 'delayed', a fact the system does not possess).
